s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent, severe, unilateral headaches with visual aura and refractory to multiple treatments
salient_findings: Unilateral headache with radiation to multiple regions
Refractory to multiple treatments, including triptans and corticosteroids
key_facts: 17-year history of migraine headaches
Right-sided migraine with visual aura
Pain behind the right eye radiating to the right frontal, temporal, and suboccipital regions
3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days
Relief only from sumatriptan
Failed trials of acetaminophen, ibuprofen, rizatriptan, methylprednisolone, prednisone, and dexamethasone
Developed a new headache pattern in January 2023
Failed treatment with ketorolac, rizatriptan, and dexamethasone taper
Failed treatment with naratriptan, prochlorperazine, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and diphenhydramine
Unremarkable brain magnetic resonance imaging
Underwent an ultrasound-guided right sphenopalatine ganglion block with bupivacaine and dexamethasone

shortlist.label: Chronic Migraine
shortlist.why_kept: 17-year history of migraine headaches, severe migraines with visual aura

shortlist.label: Hemicrania Continua
shortlist.why_kept: Unilateral headache with refractory symptoms, failed treatments

shortlist.label: Cluster Headache
shortlist.why_kept: Severe, unilateral headaches with distinct pain pattern

shortlist.label: Status Migrainosus
shortlist.why_kept: Prolonged, severe migraine episodes lasting 3 to 7 days

shortlist.label: Medication Overuse Headache
shortlist.why_kept: Frequent migraines, multiple medication trials with limited relief

raw.rationale: The patient has a 17-year history of migraine headaches with a high frequency of 3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days, which aligns with the diagnostic criteria for Chronic Migraine.

rejected.label: Hemicrania Continua
rejected.why: The patient's headache pattern is not continuous, but rather episodic, which does not fit the diagnostic criteria for Hemicrania Continua.

rejected.label: Cluster Headache
rejected.why: The patient's headache is not strictly unilateral and does not have the characteristic cluster periods, which are required for a diagnosis of Cluster Headache.

rejected.label: Status Migrainosus
rejected.why: Although the patient has had prolonged migraines, the description does not indicate a continuous migraine lasting more than 72 hours, which is necessary for a diagnosis of Status Migrainosus.

rejected.label: Medication Overuse Headache
rejected.why: There is no indication that the patient is overusing medications, and the failed trials of various medications suggest that the issue is not simply medication overuse.
